plan.title: Whole-blood subgroup discovery beyond case/control
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question is class discovery: do the 120 whole-blood samples (60 cases, 60 controls; 12,000 genes x 121 columns in counts.csv, Salmon gene-level integer counts; metadata.csv holds one condition column per sample) carry subgroup structure beyond the known case-versus-control split, and how many subgroups, and how stable are they. This is a clustering question, not a differential-expression question, so no DE test is planned.

The flow is: (T1S1) sample-structure QC on the raw counts — blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library-size and detected-gene distributions — which both screens for outliers and establishes whether condition is the dominant axis of variance. (T1S2) minimal low-count filtering with edgeR filterByExpr on the 120 samples with group = condition, then the blind VST matrix as the clustering input; normalization stays inside the model (median-of-ratios size factors), no pre-scaled counts. (T3S4) consensus clustering with ConsensusClusterPlus over k = 2..8, 1000 resamples, 80% item and 80% feature subsampling, on the top 2000 most variable VST genes, gene-centered, with Pearson distance and both hierarchical average linkage and PAM run so the partition method is stated rather than implicit; k is chosen from the consensus CDF, the relative change in area under the CDF, and the proportion of ambiguous clustering (PAC), not from delta-area alone. (T3S5) stability and confounder adjudication: a null reference from label-permuted / variance-matched simulated data to show what PAC the same pipeline returns on data with no true clusters, silhouette on the consensus distance, bootstrap/split-half cluster agreement (adjusted Rand index), and cross-tabulation of the cluster labels against condition, library size, detected genes, and per-sample missingness — because a cluster explained by depth is not a biological subgroup. (T3S6) characterization of whatever clusters survive: which genes separate them (descriptive, limma moderated t between clusters flagged explicitly as circular because the clusters were derived from the same data) and PCA loadings as a descriptive substitute for metagenes, since NMF is not installed.

Key honesty constraints written into the steps: consensus clustering returns clusters on random data, so k must be defended against a null, and any cluster is a hypothesis until an independent variable or an external cohort supports it. UMAP/t-SNE, if drawn, is a picture only — no cluster or distance claim comes from it. If PAC and the null reference show no k beats the null, the correct reported answer is 'one group beyond case/control', and the steps must state that outcome rather than force a k.

Median-of-ratios size factors with blind VST for clustering input
Consensus clustering of samples with ConsensusClusterPlus

acceptance_criteria: At least 20 null datasets processed through the identical pipeline; observed PAC and delta area plotted against the null distribution with an empirical p-value at the chosen k
Bootstrap/split-half stability reported as adjusted Rand index (distribution, not a single number) and per-cluster Jaccard stability; silhouette widths on the consensus distance reported
Cluster-by-condition contingency table with a chi-square or Fisher test and an effect size
Association of cluster label with library size, detected genes, zero fraction, and globin fraction tested with effect sizes reported
An explicit verdict per cluster: candidate biological subgroup / technical artefact / restatement of case-control / not distinguishable, with the reasoning stated
If the observed PAC does not beat the null, the step reports 'no subgroup structure beyond case/control is supported' rather than reporting a k
constraints: The null datasets must go through the exact same filtering, gene selection, centering, distance, linkage, and resampling settings as the observed data
Report effect sizes alongside every p-value
State that with only condition, library size, and detection metrics available, clusters cannot be fully cleared of unmeasured technical origin
Do not reclassify a cluster as biological on the basis of a non-significant confounder test alone
caveats: Per-gene permutation destroys co-expression, which is the correct null for 'are there clusters', but it also destroys any real shared technical axis — so it is a conservative test for biology and a liberal one for artefacts
Jaccard stability below roughly 0.6 is conventionally regarded as an unstable cluster; state the threshold used rather than assuming one
120 samples split into 3+ clusters leaves small groups whose stability estimates are wide

grounding.reason: Consensus clustering returns clusters on random data (R-0141@ac9d), so k is defended against an explicit null; clusters are tabulated against library size and processing variables before any biological claim per R-0142@c982.

steps.name: Descriptive characterization of the surviving clusters
steps.question: If any subgroup survives the stability and confounder screen, which genes and expression programs distinguish it from the other 120-sample subgroups, and does it sit inside cases, inside controls, or across both?
steps.description: Only for clusters that T3S5 called candidate biological subgroups. Compute per-cluster descriptive gene signatures: limma moderated t statistics for each cluster versus the rest on the filtered VST matrix, reporting the top genes per cluster; and PCA loadings of the leading components of the centered VST matrix as a descriptive account of the gene programs that separate the clusters. Report the composition of each cluster by condition (how many cases, how many controls). Every gene-level result here is circular — the clusters were defined from the same expression matrix, so the p-values are not valid inference — and the step must label the tables 'descriptive, circular; p-values not interpretable as evidence of differential expression'. If T3S5 supported no subgroup, this step reports that and produces only the cluster-by-condition composition table.
steps.context: Whole blood: the leading axes of variation are typically leukocyte composition (neutrophil vs lymphocyte balance), globin content, and interferon signalling. Naming which of these a cluster's top genes resemble is a useful orientation, but it is an observation about marker identity, not a deconvolution — no cell-fraction claim should be made without an actual deconvolution step, which is not planned here.
acceptance_criteria: Per-cluster top gene tables produced from limma moderated t, each explicitly labelled as circular and descriptive
PCA loadings of the leading components reported as gene programs, with the statement that a principal component mixes positive and negative weights and is not a metagene
Cluster-by-condition composition table (cases and controls per cluster) reported

If a cluster's top genes resemble a known whole-blood axis (granulocyte, lymphocyte, globin, interferon), that resemblance is stated as an observation with the marker genes named, not as a cell-fraction estimate
If no subgroup survived T3S5, the step says so and produces only the composition table
constraints: Label all cluster-versus-rest statistics as circular and non-inferential; do not report them as differential expression findings
Do not claim cell-type proportions; no deconvolution is run in this plan
Do not run this characterization on clusters T3S5 flagged as technical or as restatements of case/control, except to note that flag
caveats: Selection of clusters and testing of genes on the same samples inflates significance without bound; the tables are for orientation only
A cluster spanning both cases and controls is more likely a shared technical or compositional axis than a disease subtype

grounding.reason: NMF is absent from the environment, so PCA loadings serve as the descriptive substitute for gene programs per R-0144@dcfc, with the caution that a PC is not a metagene.

steps.name: Clustering report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the answer to the research question — how many subgroups exist beyond the case/control split among the 120 whole-blood samples, and how stable are they — stated with the full method, the evidence for k, and the reproducibility record?
steps.description: Assemble the final report. State the input matrix and its transform, the number of genes kept after filtering and the number selected for clustering with the criterion, the distance, the linkage/partition method, and the number of resamples. Give the evidence for the chosen k: consensus CDF, relative change in area, and PAC across k = 2..8, alongside the null-reference distribution from T3S5. List every sample with its cluster and item consensus, and each cluster's cluster consensus, adjusted Rand stability, and Jaccard stability. Include the cluster-by-condition table and the cluster-versus-technical-covariate table. State plainly that consensus clustering finds structure in random data, and that each reported cluster is a hypothesis until an independent variable or an external cohort supports it. Attach the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, the random seeds of every resampling step, and all package versions.
steps.context: The lead conclusion must directly answer the question asked: a number of subgroups with a stability statement, or the statement that no subgroup structure beyond case/control is supported. Do not bury either answer under method description.
acceptance_criteria: Report leads with the answer: the supported number of subgroups (or that none is supported) and their stability
Input transform, gene counts at each stage, distance, linkage/partition, and resample count are all stated
k evidence (CDF, delta area, PAC) is shown across k = 2..8 with the null reference alongside
Per-sample cluster with item consensus and per-cluster cluster consensus are listed
Cluster-by-condition and cluster-by-technical-covariate tables are included
The null-structure caution and the 'cluster is a hypothesis' statement appear in the report body
Reproducibility record includes sessionInfo, every random seed, and all package versions
constraints: Lead with the conclusion, then the evidence
Report the negative result plainly if the null reference was not beaten
Do not present the circular cluster-marker tables from T3S6 as differential expression evidence
caveats: No external cohort or independent variable is available in this dataset, so no cluster can be validated here — say so

grounding.reason: The clustering report states the input, method, k evidence, per-sample consensus, and the technical cross-tabulation per R-0152@7a42, with the reproducibility record per R-0086@becf.
